Government figures worth knowing: 31% of UK small businesses (10 to 49 staff) that store data off-site were hit by a server or cloud outage in the past year. Across all businesses it was 20%.

And this week marks a year since the big AWS outage, when a DNS fault took its main US region down for about 15 hours.

The question isn't whether to use the cloud. It's: what does your team do for those hours?

Sources: DSIT UK Business Data Survey 2026 (gov.uk); AWS post-event summary, October 2025.
ig:
31% of UK small businesses that keep data off-site were affected by a server or cloud outage in the last 12 months.

That's from the government's UK Business Data Survey 2026 (small = 10 to 49 staff; across all businesses it was 20%). And a year ago this week, a DNS fault knocked out AWS's US-East-1 region for around 15 hours, taking plenty of well-known apps with it.

The cloud is still the right choice for most. It just isn't a reason to skip a plan B:
• Know which systems you can't work without
• Keep an export or backup you can actually open
• Write down what staff do while it's down

Sources: DSIT UK Business Data Survey 2026; AWS post-event summary, Oct 2025.

li:
A year ago this week, a DNS fault in AWS's US-EAST-1 region caused a disruption lasting roughly 15 hours \(AWS post-event summary, 19–20 October 2025\).

It wasn't a one-off risk. In the UK Business Data Survey 2026 \(DSIT, published June 2026\), 31% of small businesses that store data off-site said they'd been affected by a server or cloud outage in the previous 12 months. Across all businesses, the figure was 20%.

Three practical takeaways:
→ List the systems your business can't operate without
→ Keep a recent export or backup you have actually tested opening
→ Agree a simple manual fallback, and tell staff where it's written down

Resilience doesn't need to be expensive. It needs to be decided before the bad day.

Worth knowing if you build AI workflows for clients: n8n 2.43.0 (6 Oct 2026) added an opt-in budget guardrail for agent runs, plus resumable executions.

For any client, "we cap what the AI can spend" is a reassuring line, as long as you've actually turned it on. Source: n8n v2.43.0 release notes on GitHub.
ig:
Small n8n change, big deal if you run AI on a client's account.

n8n 2.43.0 (released 6 Oct 2026) added an opt-in budget guardrail for agent runs. The same release added resumable executions at node boundaries.

Why I care: whether it's a clinic, a restaurant or an online shop, owners fear one thing about AI more than bad answers. A bill they didn't expect. A spend cap on agent runs is an easy promise to make on a sales call, as long as you actually switch it on.

It's opt-in, so check your instance version and settings before you promise it.

Source: n8n release notes, v2.43.0.

#n8n #automation #aiagents #freelancer #nocode #smallbusiness
